bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which published genome assemblies, and which replicons in each, does NCBI hold for this organism?

description: Resolve an organism to its published genome assemblies and the chromosomes, plasmids and organelles each one is made of, with every accession and length NCBI reports. This is how a pipeline starts from a SPECIES rather than from an accession somebody looked up by hand: hand the replicon accession it returns to fetch_record, with a region, to pull a window of that chromosome. Assemblies come back reference-first, so the default pick is the canonical genome.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

assembly.description: an assembly accession to take the replicons of, instead of this organism's top one. Use it to pin a pipeline to one genome build rather than to whatever is reference today.

organism.description: a scientific name, a common name, or a taxonomy id (NCBI Datasets accepts all three). "Escherichia coli", "human", "559292" are all valid.

replicons.description: list the chosen assembly's assembled molecules too. Off costs one request and answers 'which assemblies exist'; on costs two and answers 'which chromosome do I fetch'.

name: find_assemblies

accession.description: the largest replicon's nucleotide accession: for most genomes the main chromosome, and what a fetch_record node's $accession wants

assemblies.description: every current assembly NCBI publishes for the organism: accession, RefSeq or GenBank, assembly level, organism, tax id, release date and total length

assembly.description: the chosen assembly accession: the one asked for, else this organism’s reference-first top hit

length.description: that replicon’s length in bases, so a region can be chosen against a real span

organism.description: the assembly record's own organism name, canonical rather than the words that were typed

replicons.description: the chosen assembly's assembled molecules (accession, name, length and molecule type), or empty when replicons were not asked for
